rows.speaker: القائلون بأن معرفة الله لا تستفاد إلا من الهادي
rows.claim: Those who make a guide indispensable for knowing God cite this phrase as explicit proof that knowledge of God comes through a guide.
rows.anchor: القائلون بأن معرفة الله لا تستفاد إلا من الهادي تمسكوا بهذه الآية

rows.speaker: القائلون بأن معرفة الله لا تستفاد إلا من الهادي
rows.claim: They argue that purification already covers all necessary duties, so restating guidance shows that guidance to God is the mission's chief aim.
rows.anchor: يتناول جميع الأمور التي لا بد للمبعوث إليه منها ، فيدخل فيه هذه الهداية

rows.speaker: القائلون بأن معرفة الله لا تستفاد إلا من الهادي
rows.claim: They also argue that Moses concludes his address with guidance, signaling that it is the mission's noblest objective.
rows.anchor: أن موسى ختم كلامه عليه ، وذلك ينبه أيضا على أنه أشرف المقاصد من البعثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī accepts that instruction and indication can help disclose truth, but rejects the claim that knowledge is impossible without a teacher.
rows.anchor: لا نمنع أن يكون للتنبيه والإشارة معونة في الكشف عن الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowledge of God precedes obedience: the verse mentions guidance before fear and makes fear follow from it.
rows.anchor: دلت الآية على أن معرفة الله مقدمة على طاعته ، لأنه ذكر الهداية وجعل الخشية مؤخرة عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear of God depends on knowing Him; those who know God fear Him, and fear is the source of good while feeling safe invites evil.
rows.anchor: دلت الآية على أن الخشية لا تكون إلا بالمعرفة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A Prophetic saying compares the God-fearing traveler who sets out at night and reaches his destination with the one who fears God and attains good.
rows.anchor: من خاف أدلج ، ومن أدلج بلغ المنزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh denied that the miracle proved Moses truthful; Rāzī lists possible attacks on miracles, then says the following action shows Pharaoh thought this one could be matched.
rows.anchor: أن فرعون إنما منع من دلالته عن الصدق لاعتقاده أنه يمكن معارضته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī's taxonomy of objections includes possible imitation, a nondivine agent, no divine intent to authenticate, or no necessary entailment of the claimant's truth.
rows.anchor: إما لاعتقاد أنه يمكن معارضته ، أو لأنه وإن امتنعت معارضته لكنه ليس فعلا لله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two verbs distinguish denial in heart and speech from the outward display of defiance and tyranny.
rows.anchor: كذب بالقلب واللسان ، وعصى بأن أظهر التمرد والتجبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This denial and disobedience followed Moses' invitation and display of the miracle, making it different from Pharaoh's earlier rejection.
rows.anchor: تكذيبه لموسى عليها لسلام وقد دعاه وأظهر هذه المعجزة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj treats nakālan as an emphatic cognate accusative: taking Pharaoh means God made an exemplary punishment of him, like saying I leave him a severe leaving.
rows.anchor: إنه مصدر مؤكد لأن معنى أخذه الله ، نكل الله به

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ supplies an understood noun: God seized him with a seizure serving as a warning; nakāl means tankīl, like salām for taslīm.
rows.anchor: يريد أخذه الله أخذا نكالا للآخرة والأولى ، والنكال بمعنى التنكيل

rows.speaker: مجاهد والشعبي وسعيد بن جبير ومقاتل، وعطاء والكلبي عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: The two descriptions are Pharaoh's claims to divinity in 28:38 and 79:24; he was spared forty years after the first, then seized for both.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول مجاهد والشعبي وسعيد بن جبير ومقاتل ، ورواية عطاء والكلبي عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Qatāda read the punishment as torment in the hereafter and drowning in this world.
rows.anchor: الثاني : وهو قول الحسن وقتادة

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffāl identifies the later offense as Pharaoh's final boast and the earlier one as rejecting Moses after the sign; Rāzī calls this the clearest reading because the passage names these two offenses in sequence.
rows.anchor: قال القفال : وهذا كأنه هو الأظهر ، لأنه تعالى قال

rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: Al-Layth defines nakāl as an exemplary warning; its root carries prevention, as in refusing an oath or a restraining fetter.
rows.anchor: قال الليث : ( النكال ) اسم لمن جعل نكالا لعيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ordinary usage the punishment is a disgraceful spectacle that makes others refrain from repeating the offender's sin.
rows.anchor: فالنكال من العقوبة هو أعظم حتى يمتنع من سمع به عن ارتكاب مثل ذلك الذنب

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī says the answer to the condition is omitted: the people of Hell enter Hell and the people of Paradise enter Paradise, as the following destinations indicate.
rows.anchor: قال الواحدي : إنه محذوف على تقدير إذا جاءت الطامة دخل أهل النار النار

rows.speaker: مالك بن معول
rows.claim: Mālik ibn Maʿwal glosses the Great Calamity as the moment the people of Paradise and Hell each go to their destination.
rows.anchor: مالك بن معول في تفسير الطامة الكبرى ، قال : إنها إذا سبق أهل الجنة إلى الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the apodosis is the statement that Hell is the abode, with a compound condition: when the calamity comes, whoever arrives as a transgressor has Hell as his home.
rows.anchor: أن جوابه قوله : { فإن الجحيم هى المأوى } وكأنه جزاء مركب على شرطين

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some identify the transgressor who prefers worldly life as al-Naḍr and his father al-Ḥārith.
rows.anchor: منهم من قال : المراد بقوله : { طغى * وءاثر الحيواة الدنيا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī allows the passage to have been occasioned by their misconduct but rejects restricting it to them: the wording and its operative trait are general.
rows.anchor: وإن كان المراد تخصيصها به ، فبعيد لأن العبرة بعموم اللفظ لا بخصوص السبب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Transgression reflects corruption of the theoretical faculty: one who knows God recognizes his own insignificance and God's power, and therefore should not rebel.
rows.anchor: قوله صغى ، إشارة إلى فساد حال القوة النظرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Preferring worldly life reflects corruption of the practical faculty; paired with transgression, it marks maximal corruption and the unbeliever whose punishment is everlasting.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { وءاثر الحيواة الدنيا } إشارة إلى فساد حال القوة العملية

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Rāzī cites the Prophetic saying that love of the world is the root of every sin to support this diagnosis of practical corruption.
rows.anchor: لما روي عنه عليه الصلاة والسلام أنه قال : ( حب الدنيا رأس كل خطيئة )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī infers that the sinner who lacks these two defining traits is not described as having Hell for his permanent abode.
rows.anchor: وتخصيصه بهذه الحالة يدل على أن الفاسق الذي لا يكون كذلك ، لا تكون الجحيم مأوى له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may elide له after al-maʾwā because the meaning is clear, as in the command lower your gaze; Rāzī also reads it as the fitting abode for such a person.
rows.anchor: ثم حذفت الصلة لوضوح المعنى كقولك للرجل غض الطرف

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says the person considers himself independent of faith.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء : يريد عن الإيمان

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī says the person considers himself independent of God.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي : استغنى عن الله

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some take the word to mean becoming wealthy, but Rāzī rejects that sense here because the Prophet was not courting people for their wealth.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : استغنى أثرى وهو فاسد ههنا ، لأن إقبال النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام لم يكن لثروتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is valid to say he felt self-sufficient through wealth, meaning that his riches made him think he needed neither faith nor the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: ومن قال : أما من استغنى بماله فهو صحيح ، لأن المعنى أنه استغنى عن الإيمان والقرآن

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains taṣaddā as turning toward, approaching, or inclining to someone; its root evokes what stands directly in front of you.
rows.anchor: أي أنت تقبل عليه وتتعرض له وتميل إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading doubles the ṣād by assimilating the tāʾ into it.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : تصدى بالتشديد بإدغام التاء في الصاد

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads with ḍamma on the tāʾ: someone draws the Prophet toward addressing the man through his eagerness to secure his Islam.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر : تصدى ، بضم التاء ، أي تعرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing Quraysh leaders' pride over poor Muslims, Rāzī asks what warrants that pride when human life begins as a lowly drop and ends as a stinking corpse.
rows.anchor: فكأنه قيل : وأي سبب في هذا العجب والترفع مع أن أوله نطفة قذوة وآخره جيفة مذرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human creation provides evidence both for a Creator and for resurrection, answering pride and disbelief alike.
rows.anchor: فإن خلقة الإنسان تصلح لأن يستدل بها على وجود الصانع ، ولأن يستدل بها على القول بالبعث

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some commentators say this verse was revealed about ʿUtba ibn Abī Lahab.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون : نزلت الآية في عتبة بن أبي لهب

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Others identify the human as the people the Messenger attended while leaving Ibn Umm Maktūm.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون : المراد بالإنسان الذين أقبل الرسول عليهم وترك ابن أم مكتوم بسببهم

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes the target every rich person who looks down on the poor because of wealth.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون : بل المراد ذم كل غني ترفع على فقير بسبب الغنى والفقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī prefers the general reading: the criticism's cause applies broadly, the later account of human origins is general, and this reading yields greater benefit.
rows.anchor: والذي يدل على ذلك وجوه أحدها : أنه تعالى ذمهم لترفعهم فوجب أن يعم الحكم بسبب عموم العلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening is a curse, among the Arabs' harshest, and signals that the proud deserve the gravest punishment.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى : { قتل الإنسان } دعاء عليه وهي من أشنع دعواتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exclamation expresses astonishment at the extreme ingratitude that produces so many evils.
rows.anchor: وما أكفره تعجب من إفراطه في كفران نعمة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although curse and astonishment usually suit the powerless or uninformed, Rāzī explains them as familiar Arab speech conveying that these people deserve severe punishment for grave vice.
rows.anchor: أن ذلك ورد على أسلوب كلام العرب وتحقيقة ما ذكرنا أنه تعالى بين أنهم استحقوا أعظم أنواع العقاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī frames the following account around human life's three stages: beginning, middle, and end.
rows.anchor: لكل محدث ثلاث مراتب أوله ووسطه وآخره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī identifies the question about human origin as the first of the three stages he says the passage will detail.
rows.anchor: أما المرتبة الأولى : فهي قوله : { من أى شىء خلقه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is rhetorical and intended to intensify the belittling of human beings.
rows.anchor: وهو استفهام وغرضه زيادة التقرير في التحقير

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says God apportioned the human through stages from drop to clot and onward, as male or female and fortunate or wretched.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء : قدره أطوارا نطفة ثم علقة إلى آخر خلقه وذكرا أو أنثى

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj interprets it as forming the human upright, as in the account of creation in 18:37.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : المعنى قدره على الاستواء كما قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī also allows that God set each organ's quantity and qualities in the proportions suited to its benefit.
rows.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون المراد وقدر كل عضو في الكمية والكيفية بالقدر اللائق بمصلحته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discussion proceeds from human proportioning to God's facilitation of the path.
rows.anchor: ثم السبيل يسره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dafq means pouring: the water is poured or flowing, and the verb describes a single outpouring.
rows.anchor: الدفق صب الماء ، يقال : دفقت الماء ، أي صببته وهو مدفوق

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj, attributing the view to Sībawayh, takes dāfiq as possessing a flow, like other nouns describing someone by what he has.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : معناه ذو اندفاق ، كما يقال : دراع وفارس ونابل

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says the object may be named with an active participle when used as an adjective; the Hijazis do this more, as in rādiyah meaning pleasing.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء : وأهل الحجاز أفعل لهذا من غيرهم ، يجعلون المفعول فاعلا

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl defines the root as pouring out all at once and cites dāfiq khayr as an omen when a vessel spills.
rows.anchor: ذكر الخليل في الكتاب المنسوب إليه دفق الماء دفقا ودفوقا إذا انصب بمرة

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: Quṭrub likewise defines the verb as flowing or pouring out.
rows.anchor: وفي كتاب قطرب : دفق الماء يدفق إذا انصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further explanation is metaphor: the fluid's owner is called flowing because he is the one who emits it.
rows.anchor: صاحب الماء لما كان دافقا أطلق ذلك على الماء على سبيل المجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word ṣulb is read with two fatḥas or two ḍammas; four lexical forms are reported: ṣalb, ṣulb, ṣalab, and ṣālib.
rows.anchor: قرىء الصلب بفتحتين ، والصلب بضمتين ، وفيه أربع لغات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All lexicographers define a woman's tarāʾib as her chest bones where a necklace rests, with each such bone called a tarībah.
rows.anchor: ترائب المرأة عظام صدرها حيث تكون القلادة ، وكل عظم من ذلك تريبة

rows.speaker: امرؤ القيس
rows.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays's line describes the woman's polished tarāʾib, illustrating the term's poetic usage.
rows.anchor: قال امرؤ القيس : ترائبها مصقولة كالسجنجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says the child is formed from fluid issuing from the man's loins and the woman's chest bones.
rows.anchor: أن الولد مخلوق من الماء الذي يخرج من صلب الرجل وترائب المرأة

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Another view says the child is formed from fluid issuing between the man's own loins and chest bones.
rows.anchor: إنه مخلوق من الماء الذي يخرج من صلب الرجل وترائبه

rows.speaker: صاحب القول الثاني
rows.claim: The second view argues that male fluid comes only from the loins and female fluid only from the chest bones, so their combination cannot be said to exit between them.
rows.anchor: ماء الرجل خارج من الصلب فقط ، وماء المرأة خارج من الترائب فقط

rows.speaker: صاحب القول الثاني
rows.claim: He further argues that dāfiq describes the man's fluid, and the following clause says this fluid exits from between loins and chest bones, supporting a male-only source.
rows.anchor: والذي يوصف بذلك هو ماء الرجل ، ثم عطف عليه بأن وصفه بأنه يخرج

rows.speaker: القائلون بالقول الأول
rows.claim: Supporters of the first view answer that Arabic can say something comes between two separate things, and that a man and woman become like one at intercourse.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يقال للشيئين المتباينين : أنه يخرج من بين هذين خير كثير

rows.speaker: القائلون بالقول الأول
rows.claim: They answer the second argument by treating the name of one component as a name for the combined whole, since one part of the semen is flowing.
rows.anchor: هذا من باب إطلاق اسم البعض على الكل ، فلما كان أحد قسمي المني دافقا

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says the dominant man's fluid determines a boy and resemblance to his family, while the dominant woman's fluid determines resemblance to hers.
rows.anchor: إذا غلب ماء الرجل يكون الولد ذكرا ويعود شبه إليه وإلى أقاربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī says male semen alone is too little to suffice, and the report about which fluid dominates supports the first view that both fluids form the child.
rows.anchor: والذي يدل على أن الولد مخلوق من مجموع الماءين أن مني الرجل وحده صغير فلا يكفي

rows.speaker: الملحدون
rows.claim: Critics object that semen is produced from the residue of the fourth digestion and draws qualities from all body parts, as shown by general weakness after excessive intercourse.
rows.anchor: إنه إنما يتولد من فضلة الهضم الرابع ، وينفصل عن جميع أجزاء البدن

rows.speaker: الملحدون
rows.claim: They say the reading that most semen forms there is weak because most of it is nourished in the brain, as its form and the first weakness in the eyes supposedly show.
rows.anchor: بل معظم أجزائه إنما يتربى في الدماغ ، والدليل عليه أن صورته يشبه الدماغ

rows.speaker: الملحدون
rows.claim: They reject an interpretation about storage there because semen is stored in vessels coiled around the testicles.
rows.anchor: لأن مستقر المني هو أوعية المني ، وهي عروق ملتف بعضها بالبعض عند البيضتين

rows.speaker: الملحدون
rows.claim: They also object that the sensory evidence does not place the semen's exit between the loins and chest bones.
rows.anchor: وإن كان المراد أن مخرج المني هناك فهو ضعيف ، لأن الحس يدل على أنه ليس كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī replies that the brain is the chief aid in generating semen, while the brain's spinal extension lies in the loins and its branches descend toward the front of the body at the tarāʾib.
rows.anchor: أعظم الأعضاء معونة في توليد المني هو الدماغ ، والدماغ خليفة وهي النخاع وهو في الصلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This anatomical connection explains why God singled out these two regions; the critics' accounts of generation are conjecture, whereas God's speech deserves acceptance.
rows.anchor: فلهذا السبب خص الله تعالى هذين العضوين بالذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human development from a drop is especially clear evidence for a freely choosing, wise Creator because complex human arrangements emerge from simple matter.
rows.anchor: أن التركيبات العجيبة في بدن الإنسان أكثر ، فيكون تولده عن المادة البسيطة أدل على القادر المختار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sign is especially compelling because people know their own condition better than that of other things.
rows.anchor: أن اطلاع الإنسان على أحوال نفسه أكثر من اطلاعه على أحوال غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People continually witness this process in their children and other animals, strengthening the inference to the Creator.
rows.anchor: أن مشاهدة الإنسان لهذه الأحوال في أولاده وأولاد سائر الحيوانات دائمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same proof establishes resurrection: the Creator gathered dispersed matter from the parents and world to form a person, so He can reassemble the dead after their parts disperse.
rows.anchor: حدوث الإنسان إنما كان بسبب اجتماع أجزاء كانت متفرقة في بدن الوالدين

none: Qur’an verse text only; the preceding segment introduces this verse as the conclusion of the resurrection argument.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī notes that this verse, like 2:48, might be invoked to deny intercession, then refers to his earlier answer.
rows.anchor: يمكن أن يتمسك بهذه الآية في نفي الشفاعة ، كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After completing the proofs of God's oneness and resurrection, God swears another oath.
rows.anchor: لما فرغ من دليل التوحيد ، والمعاد أقسم قسما آخر

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains al-rajʿ as rain because it comes back repeatedly; Rāzī says this is a metaphorical name, not the word's literal designation.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج الرجع المطر لأنه يجيء ويتكرر

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffāl compares recurring rain to the repeated return of sound in an echo.
rows.anchor: قال القفال : كأنه من ترجيع الصوت وهو إعادته ووصل الحروف به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another proposed metaphor reflects the Arabs' belief that clouds carry water from the earth's seas and return it to the land.
rows.anchor: أن العرب كانوا يزعمون أن السحاب يحمل الماء من بحار الأرض ثم يرجعه إلى الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name may be an optimistic wish that rain will return.
rows.anchor: أنهم أرادوا التفاؤل فسموه رجعا ليرجع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may also refer to rain's recurrence every year.
rows.anchor: أن المطر يرجع في كل عام

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets the sky as bringing rain again and again.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : { والسماء ذات الرجع } أي ذات المطر يرجع لمطر بعد مطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that the sky repeatedly supplies its benefits over time.
rows.anchor: رجع السماء إعطاء الخير الذي يكون من جهتها حالا بعد حال

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says the sky returns the sun and moon after they set.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد : هو أنها ترد وترجع شمسها وقمرها بعد مغيبهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī prefers the first interpretation, rain.
rows.anchor: والقول هو الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ṣadʿ means a cleft or split; the related verb in 30:43 refers to people separating.
rows.anchor: فاعلم أن الصدع هو الشق ومنه قوله تعالى : { يومئذ يصدعون }

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the earth splits open for plants and trees.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : تنشق عن النبات والأشجار

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid identifies the clefts as mountain passes and open roads, as in 21:31.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد : هو الجبلان بينهما شق وطريق نافذ

rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: Al-Layth says ṣadʿ means plants: they split the earth, so the plants take the name of what they do.
rows.anchor: وقال الليث : الصدع نبات الأرض ، لأنه يصدع الأرض فتنصدع به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath turns from animal creation to plant creation: sky is like a father and earth like a mother, both sustaining worldly life through repeated rain and growth.
rows.anchor: فالسماء ذات الرجع كالأب ، والأرض ذات الصدع كالأم وكلاهما من النعم العظام

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffāl takes the pronoun to refer to God's report that He can revive people on the day their secrets are exposed; that report is decisive truth.
rows.anchor: ما أخبرتكم به من قدرتي على إحيائكم في اليوم

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Another view makes the pronoun refer to the Qur'an, which distinguishes truth from falsehood and is therefore also called the Furqān.
rows.anchor: أنه عائد إلى القرآن أي القرآن فاصل بين الحق والباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī prefers the first referent because a pronoun normally returns to what was mentioned earlier.
rows.anchor: والأول أولى لأن عود الضمير إلى المذكور السالف أولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A decisive word is a judgment that separates truth from falsehood, like a court ruling that ends a dispute.
rows.anchor: أي حكم ينفصل به الحق عن الباطل ، ومنه فصل الخصومات وهو قطعها بالحكم

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some commentators say the passage means the Qur'an is serious truth, not play.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض المفسرين : معناه أنه جد حق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī explains that decisive speech may be stated seriously or casually; here the explicit denial of play underscores the solemnity of the message.
rows.anchor: أن البيان الفصل قد يذكر على سبيل الجد والاهتمام بشأنه وقد يكون على غير سبيل الجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers schemed by raising doubts about resurrection, God's oneness, and the Qur'an's source, citing several familiar objections.
rows.anchor: منها بإلقاء الشبهات كقولهم : { إن هى إلا حياتنا الدنيا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their attacks also accused the Prophet of being a sorcerer, poet, or madman.
rows.anchor: ومنها بالطعن فيه بكونه ساحرا وشاعرا ومجنونا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their plots included intending to imprison or kill the Prophet.
rows.anchor: ومنها بقصد قتله على ما قاله : { وإذ يمكر بك الذين كفروا ليثبتوك أو يقتلوك }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's counter-scheme means repelling the disbelievers' plot against Muhammad by supporting him and raising his religion; an opposite act is named with its counterpart's term.
rows.anchor: دفعه تعالى كيد الكفرة عن محمد عليه الصلاة والسلام ويقابل ذلك الكيد بنصرته وإعلاء دينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī compares this reciprocal naming to scripture's expressions about forgetting God, a poet's countering ignorance with greater ignorance, and God answering deception with deception.
rows.anchor: كقوله تعالى : { نسوا الله فأنساهم أنفسهم } ( الحشر : 19 ) { يخادعون الله وهو خادعهم }

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The poet's line answers the enemy's ignorance with a greater countering ignorance, illustrating reciprocal naming.
rows.anchor: ألا لا يجهلن أحد علينا … فنجهل فوق جهل الجاهلينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that God's scheme is to let them persist in unbelief until He takes them unexpectedly.
rows.anchor: أن كيده تعالى بهم هو إمهاله إياهم على كفرهم حتى يأخذهم على غرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means not to call for their destruction or hurry it; the slight respite reassures and steadies the Messenger.
rows.anchor: أي لا تدع بهلاكهم ولا تستعجل ، ثم إنه تعالى لما أمره بإمهالهم بين أن ذلك الإمهال المأمور به قليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is repeated with different wording to give the Prophet greater reassurance and patience.
rows.anchor: فكرر وخالف بين اللفظين لزيادة التسكين من الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام والتصبر
